beats.care: Renting near Panathur, Sarjapur Road or Kogilu? Promised link roads may be years away, so check real commute times first.
beats.what: Bengaluru's 2007 master plan listed about 1,000 km of CDP roads. Deccan Herald reports most remain on paper.
beats.why: Land acquisition is slow, and owners can't be forced to accept development rights (TDR) instead of cash.

cards.body: They sit within 4 km of a planned 5.5-km road that has been stuck for years.
cards.caption: flats approved near Balagere–Panathur

cards.body: Bengaluru East City Corporation's Lokhande Snehal Sudhakar said TDR is voluntary, and some owners prefer cash. A planner said TDR isn't attractive enough in pricey areas like Varthur.
cards.title: The TDR problem

opts: Building rights given to owners in exchange for land for roads
cards.q: What is TDR in this story?
cards.why: TDR compensates owners with development rights instead of cash, but it's voluntary, so roads stall when owners refuse.

cards.q: What would fix your commute most?

hook: Why do so many of Bengaluru's *planned roads* still not exist?

learn.t: A mobility expert says Bengaluru gives only 7–9% of its area to transport, against about 20% in a well-planned city.

sources.name: Deccan Herald
sources.title: Two decades on, 85% of Bengaluru's CDP roads remain on paper

tldr: Two decades after Bengaluru planned about 1,000 km of new and wider roads, an expert says around 85% are still unbuilt.
